title: Admin - Search Admin Users - Accessibility Test Plan (WCAG 2.1 AA)
overview: Accessibility testing of the Admin User Role Management - Search Admin Users feature on the Y4J platform. This feature provides a search bar that allows Super Admins to search administrators by name or email with dynamic filtering, partial match support (3+ characters), case-insensitive matching, and clear functionality. Covers WCAG 2.1 AA compliance for keyboard navigation, screen reader compatibility, visual requirements, and dynamic content updates.

testCases.title: Search input has an accessible label
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin and navigated to the Internal Administrators page with search functionality
steps: Navigate to the admin search page
Inspect the search input field using a screen reader
Verify the input has a programmatically associated label (via <label>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby)
Verify the label clearly describes the purpose (e.g., 'Search administrators by name or email')
expectedResults: Search input has a visible label or accessible name
Screen reader announces the input purpose (e.g., 'Search administrators by name or email, edit text')
Label is programmatically associated with the input element
testCases.postconditions: Screen reader users understand the purpose of the search field

testCases.title: Search input is keyboard accessible and receives focus
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin search page is loaded
steps: Press Tab to navigate to the search input field
Verify the search input receives keyboard focus
Type a search query using the keyboard
Verify text appears in the input field
Press Backspace/Delete to modify the query
expectedResults: Search input is reachable via Tab key
Visible focus indicator appears on the input when focused
Text can be typed and edited using keyboard only
No mouse interaction is required to use the search
testCases.postconditions: Search input is fully operable via keyboard

testCases.title: Search input has visible focus indicator
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin search page is loaded
steps: Tab to the search input field
Observe the focus indicator style
Measure the contrast of the focus indicator against adjacent colors
Verify the focus indicator is not solely a color change
expectedResults: Search input displays a clearly visible focus indicator (e.g., outline, border change)
Focus indicator has at least 3:1 contrast ratio against adjacent colors
Focus indicator is distinguishable from the unfocused state
testCases.postconditions: Focus state is clearly visible to sighted keyboard users

testCases.title: Dynamic search results are announced to screen readers via aria-live
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, search input is focused, admin list is loaded
steps: Enable screen reader
Type at least 3 characters in the search input
Wait for dynamic filtering to occur
Listen for screen reader announcement of results count
Type additional characters to narrow results
Listen for updated announcement
expectedResults: Screen reader announces the number of results found (e.g., '3 administrators found')
Announcement uses aria-live='polite' so it doesn't interrupt typing
Updated result count is announced as user continues typing
User does not need to move focus to discover the result count
testCases.postconditions: Screen reader users are informed of dynamic result changes without losing focus

testCases.title: No results message is accessible when search yields no matches
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, search input is focused
steps: Type a search query that returns no results (e.g., 'zzzznonexistent')
Verify 'No admins found' message is displayed visually
Verify screen reader announces the no-results message
Check that the message uses role='status' or is within an aria-live region
expectedResults: 'No admins found' message is visually displayed
Screen reader announces the message without requiring focus change
Message is within an aria-live='polite' region or has role='status'
Message text has sufficient color contrast (4.5:1 minimum)
testCases.postconditions: All users are informed when search yields no results

testCases.title: Search input placeholder text has sufficient contrast
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, search input is empty (showing placeholder)
steps: Observe the placeholder text in the search input (e.g., 'Search by name or email...')
Use a contrast checker tool to measure placeholder text color against input background
Record the contrast ratio
expectedResults: Placeholder text has at least 4.5:1 contrast ratio against the input background
If placeholder does not meet contrast, a visible label is provided as an alternative
Placeholder text is readable for users with low vision
testCases.postconditions: Placeholder text is visually accessible

testCases.title: Clear search button/action has accessible name and keyboard support
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, search input has text entered
steps: Type text in the search input
Verify a clear button (X) or clear action appears
Tab to the clear button using keyboard
Verify screen reader announces the button name and role
Press Enter or Space to activate the clear button
Verify the search input is cleared and full list is restored
expectedResults: Clear button has an accessible name (e.g., 'Clear search', not just 'X')
Screen reader announces 'Clear search, button' or similar
Clear button is reachable via keyboard (Tab)
Enter and Space both activate the clear button
After clearing, focus remains on or returns to the search input
Full admin list is restored after clearing
testCases.postconditions: Clear functionality is fully accessible via keyboard and screen reader

testCases.title: Search input has appropriate autocomplete attribute
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, search page is loaded
steps: Inspect the search input element in developer tools
Check for the presence of type='search' or role='searchbox'
Verify the input has appropriate semantics for a search field
expectedResults: Input has type='search' or role='searchbox' to identify its purpose
Screen reader identifies the field as a search input
Browser may offer appropriate input assistance based on type
testCases.postconditions: Search input purpose is programmatically identifiable

testCases.title: Search results maintain logical tab order after filtering
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, search has been performed with results displayed
steps: Type a search query that returns multiple results
Tab from the search input to the filtered results
Verify tab order follows logical sequence through filtered admin cards
Verify no hidden/filtered cards receive focus
expectedResults: Tab order moves from search input to first visible result's interactive elements
Hidden/filtered admin cards do not receive keyboard focus
Focus order follows visual presentation order
No unexpected focus jumps to off-screen elements
testCases.postconditions: Keyboard navigation through filtered results is logical

testCases.title: Search does not create a keyboard trap
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, search page is loaded
steps: Tab to the search input
Type a search query
Press Tab to move focus away from the search input
Verify focus moves to the next logical element
Press Shift+Tab to return to the search input
Verify focus returns to the search input
expectedResults: Focus can move freely in and out of the search input
No keyboard trap exists in the search component
Tab and Shift+Tab work as expected
User can navigate away from search at any time
testCases.postconditions: Keyboard users are never trapped in the search component

testCases.title: Search text and results have sufficient color contrast
testCases.componentElement: Search input text, filtered results text
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, search has been performed with results
steps: Type text in the search input
Use a contrast checker to measure typed text color against input background
Check contrast of search result text (admin names, emails) against card background
Check contrast of any highlighted/matched text in results
expectedResults: Typed search text has at least 4.5:1 contrast ratio
Result text has at least 4.5:1 contrast ratio
Any highlighted match text maintains at least 4.5:1 contrast
All text remains readable for users with low vision
testCases.postconditions: All search-related text meets contrast requirements

testCases.title: Search highlighting does not rely on color alone
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, search results display with matched text highlighted
steps: Type a search query that matches partial text in admin names/emails
Observe how matched text is highlighted in results
View the page in grayscale mode
Verify matched text is still distinguishable without color
expectedResults: If matched text is highlighted, it uses more than just color (e.g., bold, underline, background)
In grayscale mode, highlighted text is still distinguishable from non-highlighted text
Screen reader can identify matched portions if highlighting is meaningful
testCases.postconditions: Search highlighting is accessible regardless of color perception

testCases.title: Search is functional at 200% browser zoom
testCases.componentElement: Search input and results at 200% zoom
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, search page is loaded
steps: Set browser zoom to 200%
Verify the search input is fully visible and usable
Type a search query
Verify results are displayed without horizontal scrolling
Verify the clear button (if present) is still visible and clickable
Verify 'No admins found' message is visible if no results
expectedResults: Search input is fully visible at 200% zoom
Text in search input is not clipped or hidden
Results display without requiring horizontal scroll
All interactive elements remain usable
No content overlap occurs
testCases.postconditions: Search feature is fully functional at 200% zoom

testCases.title: Search reflows correctly at 320px viewport width
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, search page is loaded
steps: Resize browser viewport to 320px width
Verify search input is fully visible without horizontal scrolling
Type a search query and verify results reflow to single column
Verify all content remains accessible
expectedResults: Search input spans available width appropriately
No horizontal scrollbar appears
Results reflow to single column layout
All functionality is preserved
testCases.postconditions: Search works correctly on narrow viewports

testCases.title: Search input has appropriate role for assistive technology
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, search page is loaded
steps: Navigate to the search input using screen reader
Verify the input role is announced (e.g., 'search', 'edit', 'textbox')
Verify the current value is announced when focused
Type text and verify the value updates are reflected
expectedResults: Screen reader announces the input role (preferably 'search' or 'searchbox')
Current value is announced when input receives focus
Input state (empty, has text) is communicated
Role, name, and value are all programmatically determinable
testCases.postconditions: Search input is properly identified by assistive technologies

testCases.title: Dynamic filtering does not steal focus from search input
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, search input is focused
steps: Place focus in the search input
Type characters one at a time
Verify focus remains in the search input as results filter dynamically
Continue typing to narrow results further
Verify focus never moves away from the input during typing
expectedResults: Focus remains in the search input throughout the typing process
No unexpected focus shift occurs when results update
User can continue typing without interruption
Context of change (filtered results) does not cause focus loss
testCases.postconditions: Users can type continuously without focus disruption

testCases.title: Search with special characters does not break accessibility
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, search input is focused
steps: Type special characters in the search input (e.g., '@', '"', '<', '>', '&')
Verify the page does not break or produce errors
Verify screen reader still functions correctly
Verify the 'No admins found' message appears if no matches
Verify no JavaScript errors or broken HTML is produced
expectedResults: Special characters are accepted in the input without errors
Page remains functional and accessible
Screen reader continues to work correctly
No broken HTML or ARIA attributes result from special character input
Appropriate no-results message is shown if applicable
testCases.postconditions: Search handles special characters gracefully without breaking accessibility

testCases.title: Search input has visible label or instructions (not placeholder only)
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, search page is loaded
steps: Observe the search input area
Check if there is a visible label above or beside the input (not just placeholder)
If only placeholder is used, verify an aria-label or visually-hidden label exists
Verify the label/instruction communicates the minimum 3-character requirement
expectedResults: Search input has a persistent visible label or an accessible hidden label
Label communicates the search purpose clearly
If minimum character requirement (3 chars) exists, it is communicated to users
Placeholder alone is not the only means of labeling
testCases.postconditions: Users understand how to use the search field

testCases.title: Search icon (if present) has appropriate accessible treatment
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, search input with icon is displayed
steps: Identify any search icon (magnifying glass) associated with the search input
If the icon is decorative (label already provides context), verify it has aria-hidden='true' or empty alt
If the icon is a clickable search button, verify it has an accessible name
Verify screen reader does not announce redundant information
expectedResults: Decorative search icon is hidden from screen readers (aria-hidden='true')
If icon is a button, it has accessible name (e.g., 'Search')
No redundant announcements (e.g., 'search search edit text')
Icon does not interfere with the input's accessible name
testCases.postconditions: Search icon is appropriately handled for assistive technologies

testCases.title: Clearing search restores full list with accessible announcement
testCases.componentElement: Search clear action and list restoration
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, search has filtered results (not showing full list)
steps: With filtered results showing, clear the search input (via clear button, select all + delete, or backspace)
Verify the full admin list is restored
Verify screen reader announces the list restoration (e.g., 'Showing all X administrators')
Verify focus remains in or near the search input
expectedResults: Full admin list is restored when search is cleared
Screen reader announces the restored state via aria-live region
Focus remains on the search input or clear button (no unexpected focus shift)
Transition from filtered to full list is smooth without page reload
testCases.postconditions: Clearing search is accessible and communicates state change

testCases.title: Search component is within a landmark region
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, search page is loaded
steps: Use screen reader landmark navigation
Verify the search component is within a search landmark (role='search') or within the main content area
Verify screen reader users can quickly navigate to the search
expectedResults: Search is within a role='search' landmark or clearly within the main landmark
Screen reader users can navigate to search via landmark shortcuts
Search landmark has an accessible label if multiple search regions exist
testCases.postconditions: Search is discoverable via landmark navigation

testCases.title: Minimum character requirement feedback is accessible
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, search input is focused
steps: Type 1-2 characters in the search input
Observe if any feedback is provided about minimum character requirement
If feedback is shown, verify it is announced by screen reader
Verify the feedback does not block or confuse the user
expectedResults: If minimum character feedback is displayed, it is accessible to screen readers
Feedback uses aria-live or is programmatically associated with the input (aria-describedby)
Message is clear (e.g., 'Enter at least 3 characters to search')
Feedback does not prevent the user from continuing to type
testCases.postconditions: Users understand the minimum character requirement
